lessons.situation: A repair request was on hold awaiting the landlord's choice of contractor, and the landlord has replied naming the contractor they want to use for the job.
lessons.action: Treat the landlord's reply as approval and as the contractor choice, so no further response to the landlord is needed. Assign the named contractor as the maintenance provider and return the request to auto mode. Then notify the tenant that the contractor will be in touch, and send the contractor the job details so they can arrange access or quote if needed.
lessons.rationale: The landlord's reply already answers the open question of who should attend, so replying again would only add noise. Assigning the provider and notifying both parties moves the job forward.

lessons.situation: A maintenance request was paused while awaiting landlord approval to send the agency's usual appliance contractor, and the landlord has since replied with a clear, unconditional approval.
lessons.action: Read the landlord's reply and, if it is an unambiguous approval, record it as approved and return the request to auto mode with no further reply to the landlord. Then move to provider selection, assign the proposed contractor, email the tenant to say the contractor will contact them to arrange a visit, and send the contractor the job details and tenant contact information.
lessons.rationale: A clear approval needs no further response to the landlord, so the job should resume automatically and go straight to contractor assignment and notifications to avoid delays.

lessons.situation: A landlord was asked to approve a minor lock repair, chased by SMS, and replied with a vague go-ahead ('needs sorting fairly soon') without naming a provider, cost limit or a firm instruction.
lessons.action: Treat a clear but informal landlord go-ahead as approval to proceed, and do not send a further reply asking for confirmation. Rewrite the task description so it tells the contractor to contact the tenant, arrange a date and time to attend, and provide a quote for the fix. Assign the maintenance provider, send the tenant and contractor notification emails with the tenant's contact details and attachments, and send the contractor an SMS prompt. Then return the request to auto mode.
lessons.rationale: The landlord has already agreed to the work, so replying again only adds delay. Converting the request into a quote-and-schedule instruction lets the contractor assess the job and moves it forward without a further approval round.

lessons.situation: A minor repair request was on hold awaiting landlord approval, the system prompted the operator to check whether a response to the landlord was needed, and the landlord replied with a brief, clear approval to go ahead.
lessons.action: Read the landlord's reply and, if it is a clear approval, do not send any further response to the landlord. Record the approval, return the request to auto mode, and move on to provider selection. Add the landlord's cost guidance to the job description, such as assuming the job is simple and cheap but quoting if it is large, so the assigned contractor and tenant see it. Then assign a provider and send the tenant and contractor notifications.
lessons.rationale: A short unambiguous approval needs no reply, and passing the landlord's scope and cost expectations to the contractor keeps the job moving without extra back-and-forth.

lessons.situation: After a quote was sent to the landlord for approval and chased once, the landlord replied with only a thumbs-up emoji and the request was flagged to check whether a response was needed or to return it to auto mode.
lessons.action: Treat a brief affirmative reply such as a thumbs-up emoji as landlord approval of the quote already put to them. Do not send the landlord a further response. Instead, instruct the contractor straight away to proceed at the quoted price, restating the work and the quoted cost, then put the job on hold with the reason 'Waiting for Provider' until the contractor confirms scheduling or completion.
lessons.rationale: The landlord's approval was clear and nothing further was needed from them, so the next step is to move the job forward with the contractor rather than ask for clarification or return the job to auto mode.
